nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31].
nodes_process.description: Setting up the traffic simulation environment using SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator. The road network connecting Qingdao and Huangdao through a tunnel in Shandong, China, is modeled, including an on-ramp, mainline, and merging area. Driving behavior parameters are calibrated based on empirical data.

nodes_process.node_name: Vehicle Location Extraction and State Representation
nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Vehicle locations (x, y) are extracted from raw traffic video frames and represented as position matrices (m_t). The position matrix also includes signal state information. For computational efficiency, down-sampling is applied. Consecutive N time steps of these matrices are stacked to form the traffic state s_t.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, 0/4 tools named, 2/3 params stated (down-sampling factor not explicit).

nodes_process.source_quote: To accommodate the input size for ramp metering, the Q-network in Mnih et al. [30] is revised as Figure 7, which consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one full connection (FC) layer for each output layer.
nodes_process.description: The Q-network architecture, a revised version of Mnih et al. [30]'s network, consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one fully connected (FC) layer for each output layer. It is designed to process the stacked traffic state matrices and output Q-values, speed, and queue length.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 0/2 tools named, all params stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: The reward r₁ after action at is defined by the following: rt = vt + wqt, μ > 0, ω < 0,
nodes_process.description: The reward function r_t is defined as a linear combination of the average speed (v_t) in the merging area and the average queue length (q_t) at the on-ramp. Positive weight mu is applied to speed, and negative weight omega to queue length, balancing mobility improvement and delay reduction.

nodes_process.source_quote: The algorithm for training the ramp metering policy is presented in Algorithm 1.
nodes_process.description: The DRL agent (ramp meter) is trained using a deep Q-learning algorithm. This involves estimating the action-value function Q* (s, a) using the Q-network, employing experience replay to store and sample data, and using a target network for stable estimation. The Adam algorithm minimizes the loss function. An e-greedy strategy is used for action selection, and a multitask learning strategy improves efficiency by simultaneously predicting speed and queue length.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 3/6 tools named, 7/10 params stated (N, T, specific random seed value missing).

nodes_process.source_quote: The second scenario adopts the PI-ALINEA method.
nodes_process.description: The PI-ALINEA method is set up as a baseline controller. It determines the ramp metering rate (r_k) for the k-th cycle by fixing the green phase length and adjusting the red phase length based on the previous cycle's red phase and downstream occupancies, aiming for a desired mainline occupancy.

nodes_process.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach.
nodes_process.description: Twenty simulation experiments are conducted for three scenarios: no control, PI-ALINEA, and the proposed DRL method. Each experiment is initialized with different random seeds to ensure robustness. The performance is evaluated by measuring travel times, speeds, queue lengths, and traffic flows.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 0/2 tools named, 1/2 params stated (specific random seed values missing).

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data.
nodes_process.description: An ablation study is performed by dividing the control area into eight subareas. The information from each subarea is systematically removed from the original preprocessed video data to generate perturbed datasets. The DRL model's performance (travel time) is then re-evaluated with these perturbed inputs to assess the impact of different spatial information.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, 0/3 tools named, 1/2 params stated (perturbation method not explicit).
